relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan, and the folio has three blocks whose whole purpose is comparison with standard nuclear physics: rem:bw-mass-decomposition-dictionary (states the goal of replacing the empirical Bethe-Weizsaecker equation with substrate-only input, and that the absolute per-isotope binding closure is open), rem:feynman-qou-comparison (contrasts the five fitted SEMF coefficients with the zero-fitted-parameter Wedderburn formula, and says the Wedderburn error tracks the shell model), and rem:q-deformed-nuclear-models-comparison (compares against q-deformed oscillator models). All three compare against 1930s-1950s phenomenology. None cites the modern effective-field-theory framework, which is the actual state of the art and the thing a referee will ask about. This document is the authoritative review of the three main nuclear EFTs (Chiral, Pionless, Halo/Cluster), their scales, ranges of applicability and the ab initio few- and many-body results built on them. It supplies no theorem the folio derives from, so it is supporting, not core — but the omission is a real weakness in a comparison section. I read the abstract, author block and table of contents opening; I did not read the body chapters, and I am not claiming any specific numerical benchmark from it.

keyResults.statement: The nuclear landscape is organised as a sequence of effective field theories (Chiral, Pionless, Halo/Cluster) connected to the Standard Model by symmetries and lattice QCD, each with its own scales and range of applicability in energy and nucleon number.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the comparison blocks a modern benchmark rather than only the semi-empirical mass formula and the shell model, and states the applicability ranges against which the folio's light-nuclei-only reach should be positioned.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; three comparison blocks benchmark only against pre-EFT phenomenology.

rem:feynman-qou-comparison contrasts the folio's zero-fitted-parameter formula with the five-coefficient SEMF; a modern EFT benchmark belongs in that comparison, and its absence is the kind of gap a referee flags first.
